title: The 18.6-yr lunar nodal cycle changes Oyashio-Kuril O2 on sigma0 26.7-27.0 by about 12 umol/kg but gives under 10% of the sigma0 26.5 O2 loss at 160 E-180 (WOD ship data, 1950-2025)
abstract: Question: CMIP6 models do not have the 18.6-year lunar nodal modulation of Kuril Strait tidal mixing. Does this cycle control oxygen (O2) at the Oyashio-Kuril source, and does it explain the freshening and O2 loss on sigma0 26.5 at 160 E-180 that climate modes and models do not explain? Approach: a plan with a recorded hash, written before the new series, used the astronomical nodal term (diurnal-tide maxima 1987.9, 2006.5, 2025.1) with no free phase. From 113,254 World Ocean Database 2023 casts (WMO squares 1314-1516) we made annual fixed-effects series with a cruise bootstrap. The primary blind test (H1) was the coefficient c of the nodal term, lagged 1.5 yr, for ship O2 on sigma0 26.8 at 40-48 N, 143-158 E (Pacific side of the Kurils; 741 cruises), with a trend and 2,000 phase-randomised surrogates (rule c > 0, p < 0.05). Results: c = +12.0 umol/kg (95% 10.1-13.9). The phase-surrogate p = 0.067, so H1 failed its rule by a small margin. The AR(1) surrogate p = 0.001. The free-phase O2 maximum comes 1.9 yr (1.5-2.4) after the nodal maximum, and the harmonic explains 40% of the detrended variance. In 2006-2025, after the original studies (Osafune and Yasuda 2006), c = +22.8 (p = 0.021). AOU, salinity and thickness on 26.7-26.9, O2 on 27.0 (p = 0.007) and Kuril winter surface salinity agree in sign and phase with strong-tide mixing. Data subsets, cell sizes, lags and the omission of each decade give c = 9.8-13.8. On the sigma0 26.5 chain the signal is weak (within-type O2 at 160 E-180: c = +2.5, p = 0.12; W winter salinity at fixed temperature: p = 0.31). The nodal term gives about 0 of the 1975-1989 to 2007-2025 changes and 9% of the 2001-2006 recovery. On 26.8 it gives 70% of the 2006-2025 O2 trend but 7% of the 1950-2025 trend. Interpretation: the nodal cycle is a large part of the variability of Oyashio-Kuril intermediate O2, but it does not cause the sigma0 26.5 outcrop freshening or the O2 loss. Its absence from CMIP6 does not explain why the models miss that loss. Short-window O2 trends on denser western subarctic classes need a nodal correction. Limitations: H1 failed under the pre-set null; four cycles in 76 yr cannot separate 18.6 yr from nearby periods; ship O2 ends in 2021; the 26.5 tests are exploratory; the path from the Kurils to the outcrop was not modelled.

Top four: new blind Oyashio-Kuril series (O2, AOU, salinity on sigma0 26.8; Kuril winter surface salinity). Bottom two: published sigma0 26.5 chain series (box W winter S', within-type O2 at 160 E-180).

Free-phase 18.613-yr fits: lag of the response maximum after the lunar-node maximum, sign-adjusted to the predicted response; marker size shows variance gained. Black: new blind series; orange: published series.

citations.reason: Fixed-effects series method, fastwod.py and its published sigma0 26.5 within-type O2 and surface series, which we tested for a nodal component. This work finds that the nodal cycle does not explain its three surface and O2 episodes.
Published late-winter surface series (boxes W, OB, OY, N, KU) used in the exploratory nodal tests. Its unexplained off-T-S-line freshening is not nodal by this work.
Winter PDO and NPI indices; its finding that climate modes do not explain the 2006-2017 freshening motivated the nodal test.
Outcrop shrank ahead of CMIP6 forced path, half from freshening that models lack. This work excludes the nodal tide as the missing process for the sigma0 26.5 freshening.
Outcrop explanation of the sigma0 26.5 O2 loss at 160 E-180. The nodal test does not offer an alternative cause for that loss.
Freshening of the outcrop region reached 400 m and was not from mixing or local E-P.
Used an 18.6-year term as a null model at CalCOFI; this work tests the nodal mechanism at its source.
